title: Running Header (Page Information Line) -- Worked Example

illustrates.quote: Guiding principles: Each braille page should generally carry a page information line (PIL) indicating the braille page number, the print page number (optional), and title or current section name. It should be easily located by the reader.

page.features: Mock-up page information line: print page number left-justified, title centred, braille page number right-justified, all on one line.

blocks.features: Print mock-up of the PIL: '25' left-justified (print page number), 'Common Native Trees' centred (title/section name), '48' right-justified (braille page number).

braille.notes: One line, verbatim. '#be' (b=2,e=5) is the print page number 25, left-justified; 'common native trees' is the centred title (lower case, per the good-practice note that capitals may be omitted); '#dh' (d=4,h=8) is the braille page number 48, right-justified.

uncertain: B004 states no fixed cells-per-line page width anywhere (unlike BANA's stated 40 cells); the exact internal spacing of this line could not be independently reconstructed beyond what the text extraction shows.
resolution: Both runs agree on content. Structural choice: print.page.runningHead/printPageNumber record the PIL's own two numbers/title for documentation (matching buildModel1's schema), and the print mock-up text is kept as a single 'other' block since it is a schematic three-field mock-up line, not real running prose Emboss's paragraph/heading formatting could build from directly. Not representable: Emboss's UKAAF running head shows the braille page number and a centred title, but never a print page number at all (standards-findings.md F-66) -- even if this harness's shared per-page furniture were enabled (it is off, see buildModel1's header comment), the print page number '25' could not be reproduced. status: not-representable (F-66).
